stage: Written during training, before final comparison images were generated or inspected
basis: The already frozen evaluation plan specifies all 16 prompt IDs at seed 101 for both models. This elaborates qualitative labels only; it does not change the generation grid, checkpoint selection or quantitative metrics.
reviewer: Single AI-assisted visual reviewer; unblinded to model identity. No human preference experiment.

criteria.recognizable_cat: A recognizable cat portrait with a coherent face; record extra or missing facial features and conspicuous anatomical or texture defects in notes.
criteria.requested_color: Visible broad coat colors agree with the full prompt. Lighting alone is not evidence of a different coat color; use uncertain when ambiguous.
criteria.requested_pattern: The requested solid, tabby or bicolor pattern is visually supported. A pattern mismatch is separate from a color mismatch.
criteria.requested_pose: Front view is approximately face-on; three-quarter view has visible obliqueness while both facial sides remain present; profile is predominantly side-on. Ambiguous intermediate views are uncertain.
criteria.plain_light_background: The background is mostly light and visually simple. A slight gradient or soft shadow is acceptable. Distinct furniture, outdoor scenery or complex texture fails; a very tightly cropped face with too little visible background is uncertain. This is a qualitative check, not a new quantitative metric.

rules: Inspect every one of the fixed 32 images, including failures and safety-filtered outputs.
Record what is visible; do not infer improvements from validation loss or automated scores.
Keep uncertain separate from met and not_met. Do not turn this small single-reviewer audit into a general accuracy estimate.
The illustrative report pairs p03 and p15 at seed 101 were selected before output inspection. Additional failure examples must be labeled as examples, not representative samples.

Nearest-training-image pairs are a separate similarity screen. Inspect the recorded highest-similarity cases without claiming that similarity proves copying or that dissimilarity proves absence of memorization.
